heroHeadline: Day 85 of Op Ghazab — TTP Commander Tor Saqib Killed in Spinwam IBO; Afghan Commander Basir Eliminated; PM Shehbaz Reaffirms 'Full Resolve'
heroSubtitle: On May 21, 2026 (Day 85 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), Pakistani security forces killed four TTP militants including wanted commander Tor Saqib (Rs3 million bounty) in an intelligence-based operation in Spinwam, North Waziristan — the second targeted IBO in 48 hours, following the May 20 killing of Afghan commander Basir in Arjam Kali NWA. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, visiting the Command and Staff College in Quetta on May 20, reaffirmed the operation is 'continuing with full resolve to defend lives and property of innocent citizens against Afghan Taliban-based terrorist proxies.' No new cross-border airstrikes into Afghanistan have been confirmed since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike — a 16-day pause — as Pakistan pivots to precision intelligence-based operations inside Pakistani territory while maintaining the 'decisive action' posture. Three journalists remain in Taliban detention: Paigard News Agency head Jawid Niazi (Day 16), TOLO News presenter Mansoor Niazi (Day 15), and political editor Imran Danish (Day 13). The CPJ's May 19 demand that the EU cancel Taliban Brussels migration talks remains unacknowledged by the European Commission. The Taliban's controversial new family law codifying child marriage (enacted May 18) has drawn condemnation from over 100 rights groups. No formal ceasefire; no Urumqi Round 2 date announced; China silent since April 8.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
